title: SSE resume handshake and partial-message reconstruction for Hosted API disconnects
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Customers have reported sessions where Hosted SSE streams disconnect mid-response and clients receive truncated or malformed partial outputs. Existing resume logic (based on Last-Event-ID) is inconsistent across client SDKs and server instances. This ticket implements a formal SSE resume handshake with checkpoint tokens plus server-side partial-message reconstruction so clients can reliably resume without duplicating or losing tokens. The work also includes migration compatibility for older clients and mitigations for transient network flaps.
acceptance_criteria: Define and publish an SSE resume handshake protocol: server-issued checkpoint token, client resume request with idempotency key, and explicit resume result codes (OK/INCOMPLETE/INVALID_TOKEN).
Server can reconstruct partial outputs from stored chunk sequence metadata and deliver a contiguous stream to resuming clients with deduplication of tokens at most-once semantics.
End-to-end tests simulating disconnects at 10k/s, verifying resume success rate >= 99.5% and zero duplicated tokens in resumed sessions.
Backward-compatible behavior: older clients without resume support still receive a deterministic DONE event and clear error guidance; no regressions for non-streaming endpoints.
Instrument metrics and dashboards: resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, resumed_duplicate_tokens, partial_reconstruction_failures and alert on regression thresholds.
Customer-facing KB doc and incident postmortem link created and reviewed by Support.
implementation_notes: Introduce checkpoint token model: short-lived opaque token (HMAC-signed) containing last_sequence_id and model_version. Store minimal chunk metadata in RocksDB for quick reconstruction.

API: when streaming, server periodically emits CHECKPOINT events with token and sequence_id. On disconnect client sends /resume with token + idempotency_key. Server validates HMAC and attempts reconstruction.

Partial-message format: include chunk_seq and total_seq fields on each data event to allow chunk reassembly and out-of-order detection. Avoid changing payload encoding (base64 if binary) to maintain SDK compatibility.
Edge cases: concurrent reconnect from multiple clients (same idempotency_key) should be serialized; use optimistic lock on token consumption with TTL of 30s to prevent duplicate consumption.

Fallback: if reconstruction fails (missing chunks due to retention), server returns INCOMPLETE with best-effort last_token and instructions for client-side re-request of remaining content via non-streaming API.
Performance: maintain memory-bound LRU for chunk metadata to keep CPU and memory overhead <5% for p99 workloads. Benchmarks required on Dedicated and Hosted fleets.
Compatibility: implement feature-flag gated rollout and header to signal resume-capable server; SDK teams will add client-side handshake support in next release.
timeline_updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket opened after escalations from three customers in last 48h. Initial triage: P0. Assigned to Marco.
2026-03-03: Spike completed — prototype handshake and checkpoint event types validated in staging. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4567
2026-03-06: Design review with SDK leads (Priya, Dan). Agreed on token HMAC scheme and chunk metadata fields. Action: engineering to implement server-side storage and APIs; SDKs to add resume call.
2026-03-08: Load tests show reconstruction algorithm adds ~2ms p95; acceptable. Need to optimize RocksDB index layout for high qps workloads.
2026-03-11: Security review flagged token expiry and replay window; adjusted to 30s TTL and single-consume semantics. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/security/pull/122
2026-03-12: Implementation underway; integration tests failing in case of multi-tenant token collision; investigating namespacing token keys per-customer.
regression_test_plan: Unit tests for token HMAC and validation logic.
Integration test: simulated client disconnect at various offsets and validate reconstructed stream matches original output bit-for-bit.
Chaos test: random packet loss + reconnect storms to assert resume_success_rate >= 99.5%.
Backward compatibility tests for SDKs that do not send resume token.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary, 10% of Hosted fleet): enable resume handshake; collect metrics for 48h.
Phase 2 (50%): SDK release coordinated with canary; enable server-side token single-consume semantics.
Phase 3 (global): enable across Hosted; notify Dedicated customers and provide migration guide for Private deployments.
Rollback: feature-flag off on server and invalidate outstanding tokens; record telemetry for root-cause analysis.
